Can you explain the main options in simple terms?
Here's a simple breakdown of the main spirit types:
Whiskey is the big family name — it includes many different styles made from grains.
Bourbon is American whiskey that must contain at least 51% corn, giving it a sweeter, smoother taste. It can only be made in the USA and nothing can be added except water.
Scotch is whiskey made exclusively in Scotland, aged for at least three years in oak casks. It often has a more complex, sometimes smoky flavor.
Tequila is completely different — it's made from the agave plant in Mexico, not grains. It has a distinctive earthy, sometimes citrusy flavor.
Think of it this way: all Scotch and Bourbon are whiskey, but not all whiskey is Scotch or Bourbon. They're part of the same family but each has its own unique character.

Is there anything else a beginner needs to get started?

Seen • Just now
Good news — you don't need much to get started! Here's what's helpful:
The Essentials:
The whiskey itself — that's your main purchase
A glass — any glass works, but if you want to do it right, a Glencairn glass or small wine glass is ideal for savoring the aroma. A regular tumbler works in a pinch, though it doesn't let you smell the whiskey as well.
Water — have spring water or soft tap water handy. Adding a few drops can soften the alcohol punch and open up the flavors, especially as a beginner.
Optional but nice:
Ice — if you want to try it "on the rocks." Big cubes melt slower and won't water it down as much.
How to start:
Try it neat (straight) first with just a small pour — about 3/4 of an ounce. Then add a bit of water to see how it changes. Skip the ice initially if you really want to taste the whiskey.
The bottom line: Just grab a bottle and use whatever glass you have at home. You can always upgrade your glassware later once you know you enjoy it.

How do I use it properly the very first time?
• Just now
Seen • Just now
Here's your simple step-by-step guide for your first time:
Before you start:
Make sure the whiskey is at room temperature
Have a glass of water nearby
Avoid coffee, smoking, or spicy food right before — you want a fresh palate
Step 1: Pour
Pour about 3/4 of an ounce (a small amount) into your glass.
Step 2: Smell (The Aroma)
Gently bring the glass up to your nose — don't rush! Take your nose away after each sniff. Trust the first thing you smell, then repeat and other layers will reveal themselves. Can you pick out vanilla, honey, or toasted wood?
Step 3: Taste (The Palate)
Take a small sip and roll it over your tongue and around your mouth. Savor the flavors — are they sweet? Spicy? Woody? Notice the texture too.
Step 4: The Finish
After you swallow, notice how long the taste lingers in your mouth. The best spirits have a lingering, enjoyable finish.
Step 5: Experiment
Repeat the process a few times — you'll notice new flavors each time. Then try adding a few drops of water to see how it changes.
The key: Take your time, don't rush, and trust what you're experiencing. There's no wrong answer!
